stage1.impression: A centred, symmetrical view of two red speakers in a timber-framed niche, seen past a wall of red velvet chair backs, with two glowing glass balls on pale tables. It reads as a CG showroom or game interior, not a photograph: the blacks are lifted and milky, the niche's block wall reads as a regular tiled grid with no pool of light on it, the speaker cabinets glow a flat salmon pink, the Orbs are blown grey spheres, and both table tops clip. As a specific place it has an idea (an altar of speakers in a red room) that a magazine might publish, but this frame reads as a generic red lounge render.

blocking_9: True blacks: frame lum_p1 under 6 and the deep shadows (ceiling, chair undersides) near black but holding detail; now lum_p1 is 12.1 and every shadow is a milky red-grey
The altar lit as a pool: the niche wall shows a visible fall-off from the spots, centre to edge range over 40; now its lum_range is 20.5 and it is flat
The Ember cabinets read as thick tinted cast acrylic with glowing edges and the white batts visible through them, not a flat pink painted surface
Orbs read as smoked acrylic with a frosted liner glowing within it, not blown grey glass balls with a hot spot; table tops not clipped
The end-grain block lining reads as timber end grain with irregular blocks and growth rings at 1:1, not a uniform tiled grid
A foreground that does not hide half the frame behind one featureless chair back, and signs of life in the zone (a glass, a record, a coat)

defects.what: lifted, milky blacks over the whole frame (lum_p1 12.1, ceiling band median 17 with p5 14); low contrast reads as CG plus haze, not night
niche back wall flat (lum_range 20.5) and its end-grain blocks read as a uniform square tile grid
left Ember cabinet glows a flat salmon pink (r 88, g 41, b 46), lit evenly from the front by its own area lamps; no edge glow, no depth through the acrylic
right Ember cabinet same flat pink; a duplicate of the left at the same exposure, symmetrical to the point of looking instanced
felt panels behind the speakers read as flat dark red rectangles with no texture; a red smear of light above each tweeter
left table top clipped (13.7 % clip, p95 251.6), white hexagon with no oak grain
right table top clipped (11 % clip, median 198)
left Orb reads as a grey glass ball with a blown centre (clip 2.8 %); no smoked tint, no frosted liner within
right Orb same, blown hot spot (clip 1.7 %), cut by the frame edge; a dark object (glass?) clipping into its right side
central chair back fills a fifth of the frame as a smooth featureless velvet surface with no pile, sheen or seam
oak plinths flat and pale with faint repeated vertical lines; look like veneered boxes
a light vertical strip at the left frame edge (median 46) from an out-of-frame surface
denoiser smear on the niche blocks and the velvet; at 1:1 the materials are waxy

changes.problem: The whole frame is milky: lifted blacks and low contrast read as a render, not a night photograph.

evidence.measured: frame lum_p1 12.1, ceiling band median 17.0 with p5 14.0, no crush anywhere; grey-red floor in every shadow

change.from: haze 0.005 per metre, exposure 1.5, AgX - Medium High Contrast
change.to: haze 0.0015 per metre, exposure 1.2, AgX - High Contrast (or a curve that puts the black point at 0)

changes.expected: deep shadows go near black with detail; the lit speakers, tables and pools separate from the dark; frame median about 24

changes.problem: The Ember cabinets are lit flat from the front by their own area lamps, so the tinted acrylic reads as pink paint rather than thick cast acrylic.

evidence.measured: median 55, r 88 g 41 b 46, even salmon over the whole face; no edge glow

change.setting: on each Ember speaker 4 x area
change.to: 0.3 W/m2, moved behind and above the cabinets as back and rim light so light passes through the acrylic and catches the polished edges

changes.expected: faces darker and deeper red with bright glowing edges and the white batts visible through; cabinet median 40 to 55 with p95 over 170 on the edges

changes.problem: The altar has no pool of light: the niche wall is lit evenly and the spots do not shape it.

evidence.measured: lum_range 20.5, median 32; y-profile of the niche 21 to 34, flat

change.to: 140 W, 2500 K, cone 18 deg, aimed to graze down the end-grain block wall behind each speaker from close to it

changes.expected: two warm pools graze the end-grain blocks, raking light shows their relief; the wall between the speakers falls to near black

changes.problem: The Orbs are blown grey balls and they clip the table tops.
changes.expected: the Orb reads as smoked acrylic with a soft frosted core; oak grain visible on the table tops; clipping only in the core

changes.problem: The Orb's smoked acrylic and frosted liner do not read; the shell is grey and the glow fills it as a hot spot.

evidence.measured: median 103, r 136 g 95 b 87; centre blown, no visible liner edge

change.setting: how rough the frosted acrylic is (Orb liner)
change.to: rougher liner (about 0.6) so it glows evenly, the outer smoked shell kept glossy with a clean window reflection

changes.expected: a dark smoked sphere with an even frosted glow inside and a crisp specular highlight on its outside

changes.problem: The central chair back blocks a fifth of the frame with featureless velvet, and the dead-centre symmetric view looks like a showroom.

evidence.measured: median 48.9, smooth flat red surface over 36,000 px with no detail

change.to: about [12.6, 1.4, 1.2] at [16.6, 3.3, 1.0], 35 mm, so the near chair is a cropped shoulder at one edge and the altar sits off centre between two chairs

changes.expected: the speakers grow in the frame, the chairs read as a row facing the altar, the view becomes a seated photographer's angle

changes.problem: The zone is unlived-in: no glass, record or coat in the listening zone.

evidence.measured: table tops bare except the Orbs

change.to: a half-full rocks glass and a record sleeve on the left table, a jacket over the arm of a near chair

changes.expected: signs of life in the foreground that catch the Orb's light

changes.problem: Denoiser smear makes the blocks, felt and velvet waxy at 1:1.

evidence.measured: block wall p5 20.2 to p95 40.7, soft mushy edges at 3x crop

change.to: 512 samples, adaptive 0.01, denoise on with albedo and normal passes, plus 1 % film grain in post

changes.expected: end-grain, felt and velvet pile resolve at 1:1

out_of_scope.request: Make the end-grain block lining irregular, with varied block sizes and visible growth rings, so it stops reading as tile
out_of_scope.why: the niche's material is the room's design, fixed by the card; it may need a texture or asset fix by the owner's designer, not a light or setting change

out_of_scope.request: Give the velvet chairs visible pile, seams and a sheen
out_of_scope.why: the seats are fixed design; a material asset change beyond the finish settings the card allows

out_of_scope.request: A frame with only one saturated colour
out_of_scope.why: the oxblood zone is the card's design; red seats around a red speaker is the brief, so the one-colour test cannot apply here

out_of_scope.request: Show the speakers' cabinets with less salmon and more deep oxblood
out_of_scope.why: the Ember colour is EARF's product and fixed; only the light on it may change (c2)
